name: uds_sid
scope_note: Complete UDS PDUs, transport-agnostic -- run over any CanBus (via UdsTester, which handles ISO-TP segmentation itself) or any message-oriented transport your UdsTester wraps. Ported from EDS's own tests/unit_runnable/test_uds_sid_conformance_vectors.c, itself an independent port of udsoncan's own test suite (MIT, Copyright (c) 2019 Pier-Yves Lessard). Says nothing about DID/DTC/routine *content* -- only the request/response envelope (echoed SID/sub-function/DID/RID, response length, NRC byte) is the ported conformance claim; EDS's own commentary on each vector is carried into its description below. Eleven of fifteen vectors assert against EDS's generic dispatcher/core-service framing and are fixture-independent -- they hold against any EDS build. Four (tagged requires_fixture) assert against a SPECIFIC test DID (0x0001), routine (0x0012), or security algorithm that EDS's own conformance test registers as a throwaway fixture and no shipped EDS example registers identically -- run those against xaloqi.tester.conformance's reference stub (which registers the same fixture deliberately, to prove the vector's mechanics independent of EDS) or a target you have configured to match.

vectors.name: unsupported_sid
vectors.description: SID 0x00 is outside ISO 14229-1's assigned range and must be rejected with the generic 3-byte negative-response form. Upstream treats this identically across six independent test files (session control, tester present, ECU reset, security access, routine control, control DTC setting, communication control) -- stronger cross-file corroboration than any single fixture.

upstream.file: test_diagnostic_session_control.py / test_tester_present.py / test_ecu_reset.py / test_security_access.py / test_routine_control.py / test_control_dtc_setting.py / test_communication_control.py (six independent files agree)

vectors.name: subfunction_not_supported_byte_exact
vectors.description: DiagnosticSessionControl with an undefined session type (0x08) must return NRC 0x12, byte-identical to udsoncan's own canned expectation of what a compliant server sends -- cross-checked against udsoncan's Response class, whose get_payload() independently encodes [0x7F, originalSID, code] as its canonical wire structure, confirming the 3-byte form itself is not an artefact of one fixture.

vectors.name: incorrect_length
vectors.description: Not ported from a literal upstream byte fixture -- udsoncan's own client never constructs an intentionally malformed request, so no such fixture exists upstream. Ported instead from ISO 14229-1 Annex A's own NRC table, using DiagnosticSessionControl's documented minimum request length.

steps.note: SID only -- missing the session-type byte

vectors.name: session_gating_nrc_0x7f
vectors.description: ControlDTCSetting requested from the Default session, where EDS's own access table restricts SID 0x85 to non-default sessions. The REQUEST bytes are upstream's own ControlDTCSetting fixture; the GATING decision (which session SID 0x85 requires) is EDS's own OEM policy choice, not an ISO 14229-1 requirement -- disclosed as such, not implied to be universal.

vectors.name: diagnostic_session_control_shape
vectors.description: Response SHAPE only: byte0=0x50 (SID+0x40), byte1=session-type echo, length=6 (SID+session+P2hi/P2lo/P2*hi/P2*lo). The P2/P2* VALUES are the target's own server config, not asserted -- upstream's own canned 0x9988/0x1234 values belong to a different, OEM-specific ECU.

steps.note: byte0=SID+0x40, byte1=session echo (remaining P2/P2* bytes not asserted)

vectors.name: suppress_bit
vectors.description: suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit set: the server must send no response frame at all.

steps.note: no response frame may be sent

vectors.name: communication_control_byte_exact
vectors.description: CommunicationControl, enable node, byte-exact. Requires a non-default session (EDS's own OEM policy, not asserted elsewhere as universal).

vectors.name: control_dtc_setting_byte_exact
vectors.description: ControlDTCSetting, 'on', byte-exact. Requires a non-default session (EDS's own OEM policy).

vectors.name: clear_dtc_byte_exact
vectors.description: ClearDiagnosticInformation, byte-exact. ISO 14229-1 §12.1.2.2 permits this in any session; EDS's own access table is stricter by OEM policy and restricts it to non-default sessions -- EXTENDED is required here for that reason, not an ISO requirement.

vectors.name: tester_present_byte_exact_both_directions
vectors.description: TesterPresent, byte-exact in both directions: a plain request gets a 2-byte echo; the suppress-bit variant gets no frame at all.

vectors.name: security_access_odd_even_routing
vectors.description: SecurityAccess odd/even sub-function routing and response SID/echo. requires_fixture: EDS's generic 0x27 dispatcher accepts any registered level and the ODD/EVEN mechanics are sub-function-agnostic, but the KEY submitted must validate against whatever algorithm the target actually runs -- EDS's conformance test stub uses a trivial XOR (key = seed XOR 0xAA, same shape as EDS's own test_service_0x27.c), not EDS's real shipped AES-128-CMAC. Run this against the reference stub (same XOR algorithm) to exercise the mechanic; running it against a real EDS example will correctly reject the computed key with NRC 0x35 (invalidKey) -- that is the target's real cryptography working as intended, not a vector failure.
vectors.fixture_note: Target must accept sub-function 0x05/0x06 and validate keys as seed XOR 0xAA (EDS's own test stub algorithm, not its shipped AES-128-CMAC).

steps.note: byte0=0x67 (SID+0x40), byte1=0x05 (sub-fn echo), remaining bytes = seed

vectors.name: read_data_by_id_shape
vectors.description: ReadDataByIdentifier response SHAPE only: byte0=0x62, bytes1-2=DID echo. requires_fixture: DID 0x0001 is EDS's own conformance-test fixture, registered by none of EDS's shipped examples (which use 0xF190/0xF18C/etc.) -- the DATA content was never the claim (EDS's own file header says so explicitly); only the echo/length envelope is.
vectors.fixture_note: Target must have DID 0x0001 registered, readable in the default session, 2 bytes.

steps.note: byte0=SID+0x40, bytes1-2=DID echo (trailing data bytes not asserted)

vectors.name: write_data_by_id_byte_exact
vectors.description: WriteDataByIdentifier, byte-exact response, plus confirmation that the exact request data bytes reached the write callback. requires_fixture: DID 0x0001 (as above) AND Level-1 security unlocked -- EDS's own C conformance test gets the unlock for free by poking internal state directly (white-box), which a black-box harness cannot do; this vector therefore prepends a real RequestSeed/SendKey exchange (same XOR algorithm as VEC-SID-27-001) rather than cheating.
vectors.fixture_note: Target must have DID 0x0001 registered (2-byte, read+write), and SecurityAccess level 1 gated by the XOR algorithm above.

vectors.name: routine_control_shape
vectors.description: RoutineControl response SHAPE only: byte0=0x71, byte1=control-type echo, bytes2-3=RID echo. requires_fixture: RID 0x0012 is EDS's own conformance-test fixture, registered by none of EDS's shipped examples. The status record content was never the claim.
vectors.fixture_note: Target must have RID 0x0012 registered, startRoutine supported, in the default session.

steps.note: byte0=SID+0x40, byte1=control-type echo, bytes2-3=RID echo (status bytes not asserted)

vectors.name: ecu_reset_byte_exact
vectors.description: Adapted reset type: upstream's own fixture uses resetType 0x55, which is neither an ISO 14229-1 Table 186 defined value (0x01-0x05) nor one EDS implements (EDS: 0x01/0x02/0x03 only). Ported using 0x01 (hardReset) instead, which both EDS and the standard accept -- the echo mechanics upstream's fixture exists to test are unchanged.
